raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## What

The router's SSE forwarding pump (`bytes_stream_to_body`) only noticed a client disconnect via `tx.send()` returning `Err`, i.e. after the next upstream chunk arrived. This races the next chunk against `tx.closed()` in a `tokio::select!`, so the pump stops the instant the client goes away.

## Why

In the common token-streaming case the pump is usually parked on `s.next().await`, waiting for the worker's next token. If the client disconnects while it waits, the old code did not notice until the next token arrived (and, when the upstream was faster than the client, up to the 64-slot channel bound of chunks could be read first). Breaking promptly lets us drop the upstream stream, which closes the worker connection so the worker can abort its own in-flight work: the connection-drop propagation that OpenAI-compatible clients and fronting proxies already expect.

## How

```rust
let chunk = tokio::select! {
    biased;
    _ = tx.closed() => break,          // client dropped: stop now
    maybe = s.next() => match maybe { Some(c) => c, None => break },
};
```

The bounded channel and its backpressure are unchanged, and the existing `tx.send().await.is_err()` break is kept as a backstop.

## Testing

Adds `bytes_stream_to_body_breaks_on_disconnect_while_upstream_pending`: it feeds one chunk, then leaves the upstream `Pending` forever, drops the client, and asserts `on_complete` fires within 500ms. Without the select! branch the pump parks on `s.next()` forever and the test trips its timeout. All existing SSE tests (passthrough, first-byte, panic propagation, backpressure-on-disconnect) are unchanged and pass.

nodes.body:
Codex review against current upstream main (2026-07-21): the disconnect handling is logically sound. Racing `tx.closed()` against a pending upstream stream closes the real leak/latency case, and the pending-stream regression test is the right proof.

There is one concrete merge blocker: the Rust lint workflow has a genuine `rustfmt` failure in the new test around the `bytes_stream_to_body(...)` assignment. Run `cargo fmt` (or apply the formatter's multiline layout), push that formatting-only fix, and rerun checks. The other aggregate/extra failures look like CI-label gating. After the format fix, I would consider this ready.

Codex follow-up ? fixed in rewritten head `5d38519bd`.

The pending-stream test call now uses the exact multiline layout required by `rustfmt`. **GitHub lint is green**, including `rustfmt experimental/sgl-router`, and the PR is mergeable. The remaining skipped aggregate suites are maintainer-gated, not patch failures.

CI follow-up: rebuilt on current main as `220577b07`. The previous maintenance/rebase failure is gone; `check-changes`, lint, and `rustfmt experimental/sgl-router` are green, and the PR is mergeable. The remaining red aggregates are solely the missing `run-ci` label. @slin1237, could you apply `run-ci` and review/trigger the router test tiers when convenient?

Thanks @shanemort1982. Closing this because it has had no updates in 91 days.

Reopen it if the work is still relevant.

Some directories moved recently, so an older branch may need retargeting:
`sgl-kernel/` -> `python/sglang/kernels/aot/`, `python/sglang/jit_kernel/`
-> `python/sglang/kernels/jit/`, `docs/` -> `docs/docs/` (`.mdx`),
`bench_serving.py` -> `benchmark/serving.py`, `test/srt/` -> `test/registered/`.

## Code Review

This pull request improves client disconnect propagation in the SSE proxy by racing the next upstream chunk against `tx.closed()` using `tokio::select!`. This ensures that the pump breaks immediately when a client disconnects, even if the upstream is currently pending or slow, allowing the upstream worker to abort its work promptly. The PR also updates existing documentation and tests, and adds a new regression test to verify this behavior. I have no feedback to provide.
